head: kham
rule: คำ is two words and a place-name habit sharing one entry: speech (1-6), gold (7), and the northern toponym (8). Among the speech senses the line that does the work is sense 2 against sense 3. Sense 2 is a word or utterance IN THE WORLD — a thing someone said, asked, promised, ruled or went back on (คำถาม, คำสั่ง, คำพิพากษา, คำมั่น, กลับคำ, คืนคำ). Sense 3 is the grammarian's คำ-, naming a CLASS OF WORD inside a description of the language, and its existing occupant คำมูล sets the pattern: คำเป็น, คำตาย, คำประสม, คำยืม, คำตั้ง, คำเติม, หน่วยคำ, ลูกคำ. The test is where the compound lives — in the mouth or in the grammar book. Sense 7 is gold and takes หอคำ, whose etymology says so outright: หอ ('หอ, วัง') + คำ ('ทองคำ').

2: คำประพันธ์
